# GEMM Worklog I: Naive to Tiled

General Matrix Multiply ($C = \alpha A B + \beta C$) is the computational nucleus of modern deep learning. We walk through a step-by-step optimization worklog from naive implementation to shared memory block tiling.

### Naive GEMM: Why It Runs at 1.3% Peak

```cuda
__global__ void gemm_naive(int M, int N, int K, const float* A, const float* B, float* C) {
    int row = blockIdx.y * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;
    int col = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;

    if (row < M && col < N) {
        float sum = 0.0f;
        for (int k = 0; k < K; ++k) {
            sum += A[row * K + k] * B[k * N + col];
        }
        C[row * N + col] = sum;
    }
}
```

**Bottleneck Analysis:**
Every inner loop iteration performs 2 global memory loads (from $A$ and $B$) for 2 floating point operations (1 multiply, 1 add = 2 FLOPs).
Operational intensity is $\frac{2 \text{ FLOPs}}{8 \text{ Bytes}} = 0.25 \text{ FLOPs/Byte}$. On an A100 GPU capable of 19.5 TFLOP/s, this limits throughput to $0.25 \times 1935 \text{ GB/s} \approx 480 \text{ GFLOP/s}$ (~1.3% of theoretical compute peak).

### 2D Shared Memory Tiling: Climbing to 36.5% Peak

By caching tiles of matrix $A$ and $B$ in fast on-chip SRAM (`__shared__`), threads reuse loaded elements `TILE_SIZE` times across the thread block:

```cuda
template<int BLOCK_SIZE>
__global__ void gemm_tiled_smem(int M, int N, int K, const float* A, const float* B, float* C) {
    __shared__ float s_a[BLOCK_SIZE][BLOCK_SIZE];
    __shared__ float s_b[BLOCK_SIZE][BLOCK_SIZE];

    int row = blockIdx.y * BLOCK_SIZE + threadIdx.y;
    int col = blockIdx.x * BLOCK_SIZE + threadIdx.x;
    float sum = 0.0f;

    for (int bk = 0; bk < K; bk += BLOCK_SIZE) {
        s_a[threadIdx.y][threadIdx.x] = A[row * K + (bk + threadIdx.x)];
        s_b[threadIdx.y][threadIdx.x] = B[(bk + threadIdx.y) * N + col];
        __syncthreads();

        for (int k = 0; k < BLOCK_SIZE; ++k) {
            sum += s_a[threadIdx.y][k] * s_b[k][threadIdx.x];
        }
        __syncthreads();
    }
    C[row * N + col] = sum;
}
```
